findings.evidence: `grep -n "IsBounded" Complete.lean` shows the hypothesis at 124/145/218/230 and the sole producer at 154, marked `private`. `grep -rn "weightPow" TauCeti/ --include=*.lean` shows no other `IsBounded (weightPow …)` lemma anywhere. `Bounded.lean:185` already has `isBounded_finsetProd (s : Finset ι) (hS : ∀ i ∈ s, IsBounded (S i)) : IsBounded (∏ i ∈ s, S i)` over a `CommMonoidWithZero`, and `Basic.lean:180` has the public `weightPow_def : weightPow T ν = ∏ i, T i ^ ν i`, so the only genuinely missing piece is the set-power step — `grep -n "IsBounded.pow\|isBounded_pow" Bounded.lean` returns nothing.
findings.fix: Export an introduction rule: add `IsBounded.pow` (from the existing `IsBounded.mul` and `isBounded_singleton`) to `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/Bounded.lean`, and a public `isBounded_weightPow : (∀ i, IsBounded (T i)) → ∀ ν, IsBounded (weightPow T ν)`, which is then `weightPow_def T ν ▸ isBounded_finsetProd _ fun i _ ↦ (h i).pow _`. The private trivial-weight lemma becomes `isBounded_weightPow fun _ ↦ isBounded_singleton 1`, so nothing else in the file changes.
findings.issue: `IsWeightFamily.continuous_coeff` (line 124), `t0Space_weightedRestrictedSubring` (line 145), `IsWeightFamily.uniformContinuous_coeff` (line 218) and `completeSpace_weightedRestrictedSubring` (line 230) all take `IsBounded (weightPow T ν)`, but the only lemma producing that hypothesis is `private isBounded_weightPow_one_weight` (line 154). A consumer with a genuine weight family has no way to satisfy it without unfolding `weightPow` into `∏ i, T i ^ ν i` and hand-rolling a set-power induction, so the round-8 generalisation is not reachable from outside this file.

summary: The exported surface is otherwise clean — no compatibility artifacts, helpers private, bodies unexposed, coercion lemmas complete and correctly annotated — but the newly generalised bounded-weight hypothesis `IsBounded (weightPow T ν)` ships with no public introduction rule, so the three general theorems are unusable for any non-trivial weight family.
